newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says lifts business order to Daiwa Bank.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says lifts business order to Daiwa Bank.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry said on Monday that it had lifted a November 1995 order for Daiwa Bank Ltd to improve its business.

In February 1996, Daiwa Bank pleaded guilty to charges of concealing a $1.1 billion loss resulting from unauthorised trades by a former executive at its New York branch and agreed to pay $340 million in fines, the largest criminal fine ever levied against a financial institution in the United States.
The charges stemmed from the conduct of its top management during the summer of 1995, when managers covered up the trading losses.
In November 1995, U.S. regulatory authorities ordered Daiwa to close its operations in the United States and instigated the lawsuits which resulted in Daiwa's guilty plea and fine.
All orders on Daiwa Bank have now been lifted, a ministry official said.
A one-year order which restricted Daiwa's overseas foreign exchange business had been automatically lifted at the end of October, he said.

On Monday, the ministry announced the lifting of two orders, one of which will allow Daiwa to open overseas branches and purchase stocks of companies affilated with Japanese firms. Daiwa Bank will also be allowed to make new overseas trust contracts as a trustee.
